## VERDICT per failure

**07 Database — `invoices are backed by ledger rows`: the INVARIANT IS CORRECT; the READER was lying. Real finding in the test, not in the data.**

Evidence that decided it — the live page (from `error-context.md`) shows **3 students / 34 ledger entries / 15 invoices**, so `34 >= 15` is true. I then instrumented the helper and got the actual parse:

```
[probe] Ledger entries RAW="LEDGER ENTRIES\n34\nAppend-only. A correction is a new entry beside the old one, never a change to it." DIGITS=["34", ","] PARSED=0
```

`/[\d,]+/` matches a **bare comma** — `\d` needs a digit, `,` does not, and the hint text ends "…the old **one,** never a change to it." So the matches were `["34", ","]`, the helper took the last, and `Number(",".replace(/,/g,""))` is `Number("")` = **0**. The ledger count was read as zero. `Number.isInteger(0)` and `0 >= 0` both pass, so the two guards in that helper could never catch it. No money bug: the tenant satisfies the invariant with room to spare.

**01 Profile200s click timeout, 08 Backup "element(s) not found", 04 "Mixed exists", 09 template-download timeout: ONE mechanism, four instances — the app tearing the Settings subtree down and rebuilding it under the pointer. Not the old `AUTH_REQUIRED` flake; I got a call log for it (06 Security, from a run I did not expect to fail):**

```
- locator resolved to <button … aria-expanded="false" …>Change PIN</button>
- attempting click action
  2 × waiting for element to be visible, enabled and stable
    - element is not stable
- retrying click action
- element was detached from the DOM, retrying
```

`element was detached from the DOM, retrying` is the whole cause: a locator that never settles presents as a bare `locator.click` timeout 200 s later, and as `element(s) not found` when it is a `toBeVisible`. Two provable holes in `settings-client.tsx`:

1. The `hasRealSettings` latch was a `useRef` — **per component instance**. Every one of the thirteen sections calls `revalidatePath("/settings")`, so the screen is torn down and rebuilt routinely and the latch resets to `false`; the next failed background read then swapped the pane for `<ErrorState>` again.
2. `isLoading` tore the pane down **ungated** — after a route refresh the cache is briefly cold and `<ScreenSkeleton>` replaced the rail, the section and the unsaved form.
3. `settings` was `{ ...(settingsData ?? {}) }` — a fresh object identity every render, and `profile-section.tsx` keys a `reset()` effect on it, so the form was re-reset on every parent render.

I could not reproduce 01 (4/4 pass, 7.7–8.8 s) and the original call logs are **unrecoverable**: `apps/web/test-results/` is shared and sibling lanes overwrite it (`zz-tmp-students-audit-…` was present when I looked).

## FIX

- `stores/settings-store.ts` — `hasRealSettings` + `markRealSettingsLoaded` moved out of the component into the module-level store, so the latch is monotonic for the **page load**, not the mount; plus `lastBackup`/`setLastBackup` so the created artefact outlives a remount. Neither is persisted.
- `settings-client.tsx` — latch read from the store, latched in an **effect** (not during render: a store write in the render phase makes React log "cannot update a component while rendering a different one", and `captureErrors` fails on any console error). `ScreenSkeleton` now gated on the same `!hasRealSettings` predicate. `settings` memoised on `settingsData`.
- `database-section.tsx` — every count row's **value** element now carries a stable id (`#db-count-ledger-entries`, …), so a number cannot be scraped out of a sentence.
- `server/actions/settings.ts` — backup now reads receipts, attendance_sessions, attendance_records, batches; one `counts` object feeds the payload, the audit row and the card, so they cannot drift.
- `backup-section.tsx` — prints all eight counts; `null` renders `—`, never `0`.

**`src/server/actions/settings-backup-artefact.test.ts`** (6 tests) — real file-backed libSQL, then **decrypts the returned blob with production `decryptBackup`**. **`src/server/actions/settings-cas-consecutive.test.ts`** (6 tests) — the sequence `cas.test.ts` never ran. Write #1 with the held base → take the returned `updatedAt` → write #2. **`tests/e2e/zz-tmp-settings-audit.spec.ts`** — `armPaneGuard` / `resetPaneEpoch` / `assertPaneNeverRemounted`: a `MutationObserver` that names a pane replacement ("replaced N× during …, sample: …") instead of leaving a click to time out at 200 s. ## Assistant (Code · Space Bunny Free · 25.3s)

_Thinking:_

**Root cause confirmed and it's definitive.**

`typescript@7.0.2` (the Go-native tsgo port) has a completely different package shape:
- `exports["."]` = `./lib/version.cjs` — a **113-byte** file that just exports a version string.
- The ONLY binary is `tsc` → `./bin/tsc` (a Go binary launcher).
- There is **no `lib/typescript.js`**, no `typescript.js` main entry, no language-service API at the traditional path.

Every conventional TypeScript language server (vscode-typescript-language-features, typescript-language-server, and the LSP integrations in Zed/Neovim/Helix) loads TypeScript by:
1. resolving the `typescript` package, then
2. requiring its **LanguageService** API — historically `lib/typescript.js`, and today `require('typescript')` expecting `createLanguageService`, `createProgram`, `sys`, etc.

Under TS 7 that require gets a 113-byte version-string module with no LanguageService, so the server cannot construct a program. What it then reports is exactly what I saw all session:
- `npm package "next@16.2.12" is not installed or doesn't exist`
- `JSX element implicitly has type 'any' because no interface 'JSX.IntrinsicElements' exists`
- `Cannot find module ... react/jsx-runtime`

**These are not missing packages. `tsc --noEmit` exits 0 on the same files.** The packages are installed; the LSP's resolver is blind because it's talking to a TypeScript that no longer has a JS language service.

So the fix options:
(a) Point the LSP at a TypeScript 5.x copy (install `typescript@5` under an alias, e.g. `typescript5`, and configure the editor to use it for diagnostics) — restores real LSP diagnostics while keeping TS 7 for the build/typecheck gate.
(b) Use tsgo's LSP. TS 7 ships an `unstable/sync` / `unstable/async` API but NOT a language server. So there is no TS7-compatible LSP available yet.
(c) Rely on `tsc --noEmit` as the only TS gate (which is what AGENTS.md already implies — eslint doesn't lint .tsx).

Let me check whether a TS5 alias exists or whether any language server is available in this environment. Also check "other langs" LSP availability as the user asked.

2. **TypeScript 7 has no tsserver.** The repo is on `typescript@7.0.2` (native Go port), whose package ships `bin: { tsc }` only — no `tsserver.js`, no `tsserverlibrary.js`, no JS compiler API. `typescript-language-server@5.3.0` drives tsserver, so it could never start against the repo's own compiler.
3. **The old pin produced phantom errors.** Pointing it at the leftover `typescript@5.9.3` tsserver *did* start it — and then flooded the repo with false diagnostics (`react@19.2.4 is not installed`, `next@16.2.12 is not installed`, cascading `JSX.IntrinsicElements`) while `tsc --noEmit` is clean. 5. **`.ts`/`.tsx` were double-claimed** by both `typescript` and `deno` — one wins, the other never initialises.
6. **"Other langs" had no entries at all**, despite the servers already being installed globally.

{
  "content": "// Cache janitor for the monorepo: size, report and wipe regenerable build/tool caches.\n// Regenerable by definition — deleting any target only costs recompute time, never data.\nimport { rm, readdir, stat } from \"node:fs/promises\";\nimport { existsSync } from \"node:fs\";\nimport path from \"node:path\";\n\nconst ROOT = process.cwd();\n\nconst TARGETS = [\n  {\n    id: \"deno-lsp\",\n    paths: [\"apps/gateway/.cache\"],\n    note: \"Deno LSP npm/registry cache (grew past 1.8 GB); refetched from esm.sh on next LSP start\",\n  },\n  {\n    id: \"next-build\",\n    paths: [\"apps/web/.next\", \"apps/product-page/.next\"],\n    note: \"Next.js build output; rebuilt by `pnpm build`\",\n  },\n  {\n    id: \"node-cache\",\n    paths: [\"node_modules/.cache\"],\n    note: \"Tool caches inside node_modules (tsx/esbuild/etc.)\",\n  },\n  {\n    id: \"coverage\",\n    paths: [\"coverage\", \"apps/web/coverage\", \"apps/gateway/coverage\"],\n    note: \"Coverage reports; regenerated by the test scripts\",\n  },\n  {\n    id: \"playwright\",\n    paths: [\"playwright-report\", \"test-results\", \"apps/web/playwright-report\", \"apps/web/test-results\"],\n    note: \"Playwright report + failure artefacts; regenerated on the next run\",\n  },\n];\n\nfunction parseArgs(argv) {\n  const opts = { apply: false, only: null, intervalMinutes: 0 };\n  for (let i = 0; i < argv.length; i += 1) {\n    const a = argv[i];\n    if (a === \"--apply\") opts.apply = true;\n    else if (a === \"--only\") opts.only = argv[++i]?.split(\",\").map((s) => s.trim()).filter(Boolean) ?? null;\n    else if (a === \"--interval\") opts.intervalMinutes = Number(argv[++i]);\n    else if (a === \"--help\") opts.help = true;\n  }\n  return opts;\n}\n\nasync function dirSize(target) {\n  let bytes = 0;\n  let files = 0;\n  const walk = async (dir) => {\n    let entries;\n    try {\n      entries = await readdir(dir, { withFileTypes: true });\n    } catch {\n      return;\n    }\n    for (const entry of entries) {\n      const full = path.join(dir, entry.name);\n      if (entry.isDirectory()) await walk(full);\n      else {\n        try {\n          const s = await stat(full);\n          bytes += s.size;\n          files += 1;\n        } catch {\n          /* raced with another process; ignore */\n        }\n      }\n    }\n  };\n  await walk(target);\n  return { bytes, files };\n}\n\nfunction resolveInsideRoot(rel) {\n  const abs = path.resolve(ROOT, rel);\n  const relFromRoot = path.relative(ROOT, abs);\n  if (relFromRoot.startsWith(\"..\") || path.isAbsolute(relFromRoot)) {\n    throw new Error(`refusing to touch a path outside the workspace: ${rel}`);\n  }\n  return abs;\n}\n\nfunction formatMb(bytes) {\n  return `${(bytes / 1024 / 1024).toFixed(1)} MB`;\n}\n\nasync function runOnce(opts) {\n  const selected = opts.only\n    ? TARGETS.filter((t) => opts.only.includes(t.id))\n    : TARGETS;\n\n  if (opts.only) {\n    const unknown = opts.only.filter((id) => !TARGETS.some((t) => t.id === id));\n    if (unknown.length > 0) {\n      console.error(`unknown target(s): ${unknown.join(\", \")}`);\n      console.error(`known: ${TARGETS.map((t) => t.id).join(\", \")}`);\n      process.exitCode = 2;\n      return 0;\n    }\n  }\n\n  const vanished = new Set();\n  const rows = [];\n  let reclaimed = 0;\n\n  for (const target of selected) {\n    for (const rel of target.paths) {\n      if ([...vanished].some((v) => rel === v || rel.startsWith(`${v}/`))) continue;\n      const abs = resolveInsideRoot(rel);\n      if (!existsSync(abs)) continue;\n      const { bytes, files } = await dirSize(abs);\n      if (bytes === 0 && files === 0) continue;\n      let status = \"would remove\";\n      if (opts.apply) {\n        await rm(abs, { recursive: true, force: true });\n        vanished.add(rel);\n        reclaimed += bytes;\n        status = \"removed\";\n      }\n      rows.push({ id: target.id, path: rel, bytes, files, status });\n    }\n  }\n\n  if (rows.length === 0) {\n    console.log(\"cache-clean: nothing to do, all targets already empty\");\n  } else {\n    console.log(`cache-clean  mode=${opts.apply ? \"APPLY\" : \"DRY-RUN\"}`);\n    for (const r of rows) {\n      console.log(`  ${r.status.padEnd(11)} ${r.id.padEnd(11)} ${formatMb(r.bytes).padStart(10)}  ${String(r.files).padStart(7)} files  ${r.path}`);\n    }\n    if (opts.apply) {\n      console.log(`  total reclaimed: ${formatMb(reclaimed)}`);\n    } else {\n      const total = rows.reduce((sum, r) => sum + r.bytes, 0);\n      console.log(`  total reclaimable: ${formatMb(total)}  (re-run with --apply to free it)`);\n    }\n  }\n\n  for (const target of selected) {\n    if (rows.some((r) => r.id === target.id)) console.log(`  note[${target.id}]: ${target.note}`);\n  }\n\n  return reclaimed;\n}\n\nconst opts = parseArgs(process.argv.slice(2));\n\nif (opts.help) {\n  console.log(\"Usage: node scripts/cache-clean.mjs [--apply] [--only id,id] [--interval minutes]\");\n  console.log(`Targets: ${TARGETS.map((t) => t.id).join(\", \")}`);\n  process.exit(0);\n}\n\nawait runOnce(opts);\n\nif (opts.intervalMinutes > 0) {\n  const ms = opts.intervalMinutes * 60_000;\n  console.log(`cache-clean: repeating every ${opts.intervalMinutes} minute(s); Ctrl-C to stop`);\n  setInterval(() => {\n    runOnce(opts).catch((err) => console.error(\"cache-clean:\", err.message));\n  }, ms);\n}",
  "filePath": "Z:\\Projects\\buddysaradhi\\buddysaradhi\\scripts\\cache-clean.mjs"
}

  "content": "<#\n.SYNOPSIS\n  Registers (or removes) a Windows Scheduled Task that prunes regenerable caches.\n.DESCRIPTION\n  The periodic run deliberately excludes the next-build target: apps/web/.next is\n  the live artefact for `next start`, and deleting it under a running server breaks\n  the app. Prune that one manually with `pnpm cache:clean:apply --only next-build`\n  when no server is running.\n#>\nparam(\n  [switch]$Install,\n  [switch]$Uninstall,\n  [int]$IntervalMinutes = 30\n)\n\n$ErrorActionPreference = 'Stop'\n$TaskName = 'Buddysaradhi-CacheClean'\n$RepoRoot = Split-Path -Parent $PSScriptRoot\n$SafeTargets = 'deno-lsp,node-cache,coverage,playwright'\n\nfunction Get-NodePath {\n  $node = Get-Command node -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue\n  if (-not $node) { throw 'node not found on PATH; cannot schedule the cache cleaner' }\n  return $node.Source\n}\n\nif ($Uninstall) {\n  if (Get-ScheduledTask -TaskName $TaskName -ErrorAction SilentlyContinue) {\n    Unregister-ScheduledTask -TaskName $TaskName -Confirm:$false\n    Write-Output \"removed scheduled task: $TaskName\"\n  } else {\n    Write-Output \"no scheduled task named $TaskName\"\n  }\n  exit 0\n}\n\nif (-not $Install) {\n  Write-Output 'nothing to do: pass -Install to register the task, or -Uninstall to remove it'\n  Write-Output \"targets that will be pruned every $IntervalMinutes minute(s): $SafeTargets\"\n  exit 0\n}\n\n$nodeExe = Get-NodePath\n$script = Join-Path $PSScriptRoot 'cache-clean.mjs'\n\n$action = New-ScheduledTaskAction `\n  -Execute $nodeExe `\n  -Argument \"`\"$script`\" --apply --only $SafeTargets\" `\n  -WorkingDirectory $RepoRoot\n\n$trigger = New-ScheduledTaskTrigger -Once -At (Get-Date).AddMinutes($IntervalMinutes) `\n  -RepetitionInterval (New-TimeSpan -Minutes $IntervalMinutes)\n\n$settings = New-ScheduledTaskSettingsSet `\n  -AllowStartIfOnBatteries `\n  -DontStopIfGoingOnBatteries `\n  -StartWhenAvailable `\n  -ExecutionTimeLimit (New-TimeSpan -Minutes 10) `\n  -MultipleInstances IgnoreNew\n\nRegister-ScheduledTask -TaskName $TaskName -Action $action -Trigger $trigger -Settings $settings `\n  -Description 'Prunes regenerable caches (.cache, node_modules/.cache, coverage, playwright) for the Buddysaradhi monorepo.' -Force | Out-Null\n\nWrite-Output \"installed scheduled task: $TaskName\"\nWrite-Output \"  interval : every $IntervalMinutes minute(s)\"\nWrite-Output \"  node     : $nodeExe\"\nWrite-Output \"  workdir  : $RepoRoot\"\nWrite-Output \"  targets  : $SafeTargets\"\nWrite-Output \"  excludes : next-build (apps/web/.next may be serving a live `next start`)\"",
  "filePath": "Z:\\Projects\\buddysaradhi\\buddysaradhi\\scripts\\cache-clean-schedule.ps1"
}
